title: Real Estate in a Pandemic: Renters and Landlords (Part 2)

reader_summary.headline: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast. This episode is the second in a two-part series that examines the pandemic's impact on real estate. Part one focused on prospective homebuyers, sellers, and existing homeowners, while this episode, Part 2, addresses renters and landlords.

key_points.text: The conversation features A16Z general partner Connie Chan, whose experience as a landlord herself has fueled her interest in residential real estate and technology.
key_points.evidence_quote: The conversation features A16Z general partner Connie Chan, whose experience as a landlord herself has fueled her interest in residential real estate and technology.

key_points.text: Professor Richard Green, the director of USC's Lusk Center for Real Estate, and Adina Heffitz, CEO of Divi Homes.
key_points.evidence_quote: Professor Richard Green, the director of USC's Lusk Center for Real Estate, and Adina Heffitz, CEO of Divi Homes, a company that allows people to build up equity while renting a home with the option to eventually buy it.

key_points.text: We begin with the pressures on renters and the uncertainty around federal relief measures, as well as a cascading effect on mom-and-pop landlords.
key_points.evidence_quote: We begin with the pressures on renters and the uncertainty around federal relief measures, as well as a cascading effect on mom-and-pop landlords.

key_points.text: Then we turned to the outlook for prices and volume in the rental market, particularly in large cities like New York and San Francisco.
key_points.evidence_quote: Then we turned to the outlook for prices and volume in the rental market, particularly in large cities like New York and San Francisco.

thesis: The episode examines the pandemic's impact on real estate, specifically focusing on the pressures facing renters and landlords, the uncertainty surrounding federal relief measures, and the cascading effects on mom-and-pop landlords. It further discusses the outlook for rental market prices and volume in large cities, the slowdown in new supply due to construction bans and land acquisition hesitancy, and the opportunity for technology to address outdated processes.
